recent_works.title: Mobility of Persistent Solvent-Rich Phases Governs Deposit Morphology in Electrospray Deposition
recent_works.abstract: In electrospray deposition (ESD), a high voltage atomizes a flowing solution into charged microdroplets. The self-repulsive droplets evaporate as they approach the target grounded substrate, depositing the solids and carried charge. In the self-limiting electrospray deposition (SLED) regime, manipulation of the electrostatic repulsion, hydrodynamic forces, and evaporation kinetics results in the accumulation of deposited charge and conformal coating complex 2D and 3D architectures. This is a useful property for a wide range of coatings; however, SLED has previously only been achieved for a narrow range of insulating materials. Here, we hypothesize that SLED is only possible when (1) the arriving charged solvent is rendered immobile either through absorption into the free volume of an amorphous solute or the open pores/surface of a dispersant, and (2) the solvent itself is not capable of ionic dissipation (e.g., water). recent_works.title: Prediction of Single-Frequency 2D Viscoelastic Brain White Matter Properties Using an Ensemble of Forward Machine Learning Regression Models
recent_works.venue: Journal of Engineering and Science in Medical Diagnostics and Therapy
recent_works.abstract: Abstract Experimental characterization of brain white matter (BWM) using magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and numerical modeling is expensive, time-consuming, and constrained by computational limitations and model approximations. To address the scarcity of high-fidelity data, this study develops a machine learning (ML) workflow to predict single-frequency viscoelastic properties, specifically the homogenized storage modulus, of BWM. The dataset originates from a sensitivity study conducted in house where BWM was modeled as a two-dimensional (2D) triphasic composite of axons, myelin, and glial matrix. The triphasic unidirectional composite only considers 2D mechanics and diffusion in the transverse plane (perpendicular to axonal direction). Microstructural properties such as fiber volume fraction, intrinsic phase moduli, and axonal geometry were used as features for the ML model. Ensembles of regression and decision tree-based models, coupled with hyperparameter optimization, were explored, with model interpretation performed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. recent_works.title: Mechanical Characterization of In-Situ Exfoliated Graphite Into Graphene Within Polyethylene Terephthalate via the Use of a Novel Single Screw Extruder Design
recent_works.abstract: Abstract In this study, by using a novel single screw extruder design that provides a high, uniform shear environment using elongational flow, polyethylene terephthalate (PET) polymer and graphite are mixed without needing to exfoliate the graphite into graphene first. The material experiences uniform shear during this process, separating the graphitic layers by breaking up the van der Waals forces between the graphite sheets, producing in-situ exfoliated graphene and graphite within PET (GPET). Two concentrations of GPET were made, 10 and 40 wt.% GPET and compared to the as-bought PET. These samples were molded into ASTM D638 type V dog-bone specimens, tested in tension, and evaluated under a microscope. When testing the GPET samples, it was found that the tensile modulus increases with the addition of filler while the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) decreases. Microscopy reveals a skin-core structure within the injected molded samples. An outer, more ductile skin is present with a rigid interior formed by the higher concentration of graphite flakes. recent_works.title: Machine learning based prediction of single-frequency viscoelastic brain white matter – A data science framework
recent_works.abstract: Characterizing brain white matter (BWM) using in vivo Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) and Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) is a costly, time-intensive process. Numerical modeling approaches, such as finite element models (FEMs), also face limitations in fidelity, computational resources, and accurately capturing the complex bio-physical behavior of brain tissues. To address the scarcity of experimental data, researchers are exploring machine learning (ML) as a surrogate for predicting the mechanical properties of brain tissues. Here in, an ML workflow is proposed for predicting the homogenized viscoelastic properties of BWM using FEM-derived data. The synthetic FE dataset originates from a sensitivity analysis, whereby a triphasic 2D composite model, consisting of axons, myelin, and glial matrix, was used to simulate transverse mechanical behavior under harmonic shear stress. This dataset is utilized to train and validate machine learning models aimed at predicting the frequency-dependent mechanical response. recent_works.title: Deep Neural Network Hybrid Simulations to Evaluate the Poynting Effect in 3D Ogden Hyperelastic Modeling of Brain White Matter
recent_works.venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
recent_works.abstract: • A novel Hybrid deep 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)/ ML-FEM framework has been developed to predict and quantify the Poynting effect (PE) in Ogden hyperleastically (HE) modeled brain white matter (BWM). • Overcomes FEM limitations such as high computational cost, mesh failures, and instability. • 3D ResNet accurately predicts stress and stiffness tensors in triphasic BWM under shear. • Efficiently models shear boundary conditions, intrinsic material properties, and interfacial microstructures. • Proposed Hybrid PE model enables 24x faster simulations, reducing FEM computational costs. Framework improves computational efficiency in soft tissue biomechanics and traumatic brain injury (TBI) modeling. Modeling and characterization of brain white matter (BWM) are challenging due to its anisotropic 3D microarchitecture and complex interactions among the constituent phases of axons, myelin, and glia. Shear biomechanics is critical for understanding traumatic brain injury (TBI), as shear forces dominate during such events.
